open_points.subject: upload-head body failure and owner-session arrival
open_points.text: “an upload's head — hands the request on all the same, with no CSRF value and no values: the session check admits the owner's, restarting the session's 30 minutes when it is valid” contradicts “an upload […] arrives when that head […] has been read”
open_points.question: When reading an upload head fails before the head has been read, has the owner request arrived for purposes of admission and restarting the session's idle period?
options: Treat the failed head as an arrived owner request, admit a valid session and restart its 30 minutes.
Treat the request as not yet arrived, do not run the session check and do not restart its 30 minutes.
open_points.default_guess: Treat it as not arrived, following A13's upload-specific arrival definition.

witness.initial: A valid owner session is one second short of its 30-minute idle limit.
events: The owner sends an upload whose framing headers are accepted.
Reading the upload head fails before the complete head has been read.
The owner sends another valid request two seconds later.
outcomes: The failed upload restarted the idle period, so the later request is admitted.
The failed upload never arrived in A13's sense, so the session reached its idle limit and the later request is refused.
witness.observer: The owner sees whether the later request is served or requires sign-in.

open_points.subject: failed reading of the sign-in form
open_points.text: “A surface whose reading of a body fails — a form […] — hands the request on all the same […] the session check admits the owner's […] and it is refused at stage (1) as a change without its CSRF value” conflicts with “Sign-in is the one owner request made without a session: it is checked for the credential and the lockout only, carries no CSRF value”
open_points.question: Does the new failed-form rule include the sign-in form, and if so is its absent credential processed as a counted sign-in refusal or as a failed owner-session/CSRF check?
options: Exclude sign-in from this rule and process the unread body as a missing credential under A13 rules 3 and 4.
Include sign-in in this rule and refuse it through the owner-session/CSRF path without applying the sign-in counter.
Define a separate body-read failure for sign-in and state whether it increments the refusal counter.
open_points.default_guess: Exclude sign-in from the session-and-CSRF path and count the absent credential as a refused sign-in.

witness.initial: The instance has recorded four wrong-or-missing-credential sign-in refusals within the last 15 minutes and has no owner session.
events: The owner submits a sign-in request whose framing headers are accepted but whose form body cannot be read.
The owner immediately submits a well-formed sign-in with the correct credential.
outcomes: The unread form counts as the fifth missing-credential refusal, starts lockout, and the correct sign-in is refused.
The unread form is handled as a session or CSRF failure, does not start sign-in lockout, and the correct sign-in is accepted.
witness.observer: The owner sees whether the correct sign-in succeeds.

open_points.subject: service request whose body cannot be read
open_points.question: What failure does `operations` produce for a service request handed on with no values after its body cannot be read, and at which check stage is that failure decided?
options: Refuse it at stage (4) for its missing required values.
Produce a distinct unreadable-or-malformed-body refusal before value validation.
Close the connection without a Registry answer.
Specify an operation-dependent result for requests whose required inputs differ.
open_points.default_guess: Produce a distinct malformed-body refusal after authentication and rights checks, then close the connection after attempting to send it.

witness.initial: A service has a valid token and is entitled to call the routed operation.
events: The service sends a request whose framing headers are accepted.
The body stream fails before its values can be read.
The service waits for the response.
outcomes: The service receives the ordinary stage-(4) missing-values refusal.
The service receives a distinct malformed-body refusal selected later by `serve_service_request`.
witness.observer: The calling service sees a different refusal and may handle or retry it differently.

open_points.subject: sending the failure answer and closing the connection
open_points.text: “the answer is sent if the connection still takes it, and the connection is then closed”
open_points.question: Which module and capability attempt the send, determine that the connection still takes it, and close the connection after a body-read failure?
options: `instance_lifecycle` owns a listener capability that attempts the send and closes the connection.
Each surface returns a response-and-close disposition to `instance_lifecycle`.
`service_api` and `owner_interface` each directly send and close their connections.
open_points.default_guess: Have each surface return a response-and-close disposition, with `instance_lifecycle` performing the transport send and close.
